title: Buying Criteria Scenarios: SLAs, Isolation, and Predictable Throughput for Dedicated Capacity
content:
Purpose
This doc is a tactical messaging + scenario playbook for field and sales-engineering to use when engaging procurement and platform engineering buyers evaluating dedicated inference capacity. Focus: SLAs, isolation guarantees, predictable throughput, and how to structure procurement asks and fallbacks.

Audience notes
- Primary: Platform architects, infra procurement, SRE leads.
- Secondary: CTO/CPO, Finance procurement team, InfoSec if isolation is required.

Top-level buyer criteria (hypothesis)
1) Predictable throughput: sustained tokens/sec or requests/sec guarantee during business hours and peak events.
2) Isolation: single-tenant pools (logical or physical), data-path guarantees, and auditability.
3) SLO/SLA alignment: measurable uptime and latency percentiles, with credits and remediation steps.
4) Cost predictability: committed spend with clear burst policies and overage handling.
5) Operational handoff: runbook, playbooks, and escalation contacts for incidents.

Real-world buyer scenarios (to tune messaging for):
A) Fintech real-time scoring (low latency, predictable): emphasize latency p99 guarantees, colocated region support, and automatic fallback to lower-cost variant with preserved API contract.
B) Healthcare batch inference (isolation + compliance): highlight VPC/private control plane, KMS integration, audit logs retention options, and on-prem or air-gapped deployment options.
C) Consumer-facing chat at scale (throughput + burst): emphasize reserved GPU pools, autoscale/burst policy definitions, and billing for burst vs committed baseline.

Positioning pillars & single-line leads
- Economic predictability: "Committed capacity with engineered fallbacks — predictable unit economics for production inference."
- Safe isolation: "Single-tenant pools and private control plane for regulated workloads and stronger compliance postures."
- Production-grade availability: "SLA-backed latency and uptime targets, with proven runbooks and escalation channels."

Key messages per buyer persona
- Platform Architect: Here’s how dedicated capacity maps to your SLOs: predictable qps, KV cache locality, and deterministic scheduling for tail latency. We provide telemetry hooks and per-route tracing so you can align app-level SLOs to model endpoints.
- Procurement/Finance: Commitments reduce per-token variance and cap month-to-month spend. Burst is charged transparently and we provide a predictable amortized rate for budgeting.
- Security/Compliance: The private control plane + VPC option keeps control in your network, supports KMS/HSM, and audit logs for long-term retention or eDiscovery.

Competitive reframing (short bullets)
- Big cloud vendors: cheaper per-hour raw GPU but noisy neighbors and hidden queuing; we win on predictable tail latency and inference-specific autoscaling.
- Generic endpoint services: focus on model dev; we focus on production inference economics and deterministic performance.
- Self-hosting: total control but high ops cost; our Dedicated offering reduces ops burden while retaining isolation and contractual guarantees.

Suggested SLA language (field copy)
- Uptime: 99.95% monthly availability for dedicated capacity control-plane and serving endpoints, excluding scheduled maintenance with 72h notice.
- Latency SLO: p95 inference completion within X ms for configured profile; p99 within Y ms. Define X/Y per SKU profile.
- Throughput guarantee: baseline committed throughput of N tokens/sec per reserved slab with steady-state and burst definitions.
- Credits: Service credits tiered by % downtime. Latency breach triggers joint RCA and credit defined as percentage of monthly fee.

Negotiation levers and fallbacks (playbook)
- Start: propose baseline commitment + 20% burst pool at defined rate.
- If customer needs stronger isolation: escalate to physical tenancy add-on (higher price).
- If latency SLO request is lower than default: offer pre-warm option (KV warmers) and dedicated fast-path kernel enabled for extra fee.
- For procurement concerned about upgrades: include versioning & rollback SLA (model compatibility windows, 90-day staged rollouts).

Objection handling snippets
- "We can just run on cloud VMs": True, but we’ll show a side-by-side demo of tail latency under mixed workloads and the chargeback math at scale.
- "What if my usage spikes more than committed?": We support transparent burst pricing and can auto-scale into a paid burst pool; we also offer auto-fallback to compatible cheaper model variants to keep requests served.
- "We need physical separation": Offer Premium Isolation addendum (physical pools + dedicated networking).

Field assets to create / required collateral
- 1-pager: "Commitment vs Burst — How pricing maps to predictability" (finance-facing).
- SRE playbook: incident runbook for dedicated capacity + escalation matrix.
- Technical appendix: per-SKU latency/throughput profiles and recommended workload mappings.
- Procurement-ready clause templates: SLA, data isolation addendum, exit/transition plan.

Sample procurement checklist (for sales to send to buyer)
- Baseline committed throughput (tokens/sec or rps) defined? [Y/N]
- Required geographic regions & AZs specified? [Y/N]
- Isolation: logical or physical tenancy? [Choose]
- Retention & audit log requirements mapped to plan? [Y/N]
- KMS/HSM integration required? [Y/N]
- Escrow/exit plan and model artifacts transfer defined? [Y/N]

Sample lead-in email for procurement (editable)
Hi [Procurement lead],

Following up on our conversation — attached is the dedicated capacity outline showing committed throughput, burst options, SLA language, and isolation addenda. We’ve mapped your primary concerns (latency p99, single-tenant pools, and predictable monthly spend) to product SKUs. Would you like a 30-min session to walk the legal and SRE teams through the SLA wording?

Thanks,
Aisha (Redwood Inference)

Open questions / TODOs
- Define concrete X/Y ms latency numbers per SKU (action: eng-serving-runtime to publish perf matrix — jira ENG-4123).
- Formalize physical tenancy pricing bands and sample contract language (finance/legal).
- Create quick benchmark deck that shows p99 latency under mixed noisy-tenant workloads vs our dedicated pools.

Notes to self (field UX)
- Keep messaging short: procurement wants cost math and concrete failure modes + remediation. Avoid generic performance boasts.
- Use customer success stories (anonymized) that show predictable scaling during spikes — visuals win.
- Build a one-click checklist PDF to hand to procurement during first commercial meeting.

Appendix: quick negotiation script (sales-engineer friendly)
1) Ask: "What is your actual worst-case QPS and acceptable p99 latency?" Document it.
2) Present: committed slab that maps to 80% of peak; propose burst policy for headroom.
3) Clarify: isolation level required, and what compliance docs are needed.
4) Close: offer pilot with a time-boxed SLA (30 days) to validate metrics, convertible to annual reserved contract.

-- End of draft --
